meta.title: Post-independence armed and large-scale violent conflicts in India
meta.geographicNote: Republic of India including territories as they appear in standard conflict datasets. Jammu & Kashmir, Aksai Chin, Arunachal Pradesh (China claim), and Siachen are disputed; this file records locations as claimed/administered without taking a position.

scaleDefinition.small: Best-estimate deaths <100 AND duration <1 year AND geography of a few districts or less — unless flagged otherwise by type.
scaleDefinition.medium: Deaths 100–999 OR organized armed campaign ≥3 years below 1000 total deaths OR IDPs 10000–49999.
scaleDefinition.large: Deaths ≥1000 (any sourced best/official figure, rivals shown in sources) OR ≥1 UCDP war year OR COW war OR IDPs ≥50000 with lethal violence.

meta.rules: Do not treat a single death integer as ground truth. Use sources[]. Casualty figures live in sources, not as invented numeric fields. Null means unknown or not applicable, not zero.

conflicts.name: Partition mass violence
conflicts.summary: Mass killing and forced migration accompanying the 1947 partition of British India. Violence peaked around August–September 1947 and continued after 15 August, especially in Punjab. Death estimates range from about 200,000 to 2 million; displacement around 10–15 million. Not a state-versus-state war.
actors: nascent India and Pakistan security forces (uneven)
sources: Talbot, Ian; Brass, Paul; Butalia, Urvashi; Khan, Yasmin — death range 200,000–2,000,000 is the standard scholarly band
Wikipedia/secondary compilations citing the same range; no census exists

conflicts.name: Junagadh accession crisis
conflicts.summary: Muslim Nawab acceded to Pakistan; Hindu-majority Kathiawar state. India blockaded; Nawab fled; February 1948 plebiscite reported ~99% for India. Pakistan's claim remains on paper. Limited organized combat relative to Hyderabad.
externalSupport: Pakistan (accession accepted; no sustained military campaign)
sources: V.P. Menon, The Story of the Integration of the Indian States
Government of India White Paper on Indian States (1950)

conflicts.name: First Kashmir War
conflicts.summary: Tribal lashkars entered the princely state in October 1947; Maharaja Hari Singh signed an Instrument of Accession to India (Pakistan disputes validity); Indian troops airlifted to Srinagar 27 October. UN-brokered ceasefire 1 January 1949 created the Ceasefire Line (later LoC). Both states still claim the whole territory.
externalSupport: Pakistan (India: state-directed invasion; Pakistan: tribal volunteers / later regulars)
sources: Correlates of War Inter-State War #147
UCDP/PRIO ACD interstate India–Pakistan
Indian military deaths commonly ~1,100–1,500; Pakistani/tribal figures more uncertain (some compilations ~6,000 — treat as unverified)
UNCIP ceasefire 1 Jan 1949

conflicts.name: Hyderabad annexation and aftermath
conflicts.summary: Indian Army operation 13–17 September 1948 ended the Nizam's bid to stay independent and defeated Razakars. Combat deaths were in the low thousands or less. The Sunderlal Committee estimated 27,000–40,000 killed in cold blood during and after the operation, mostly Muslims in Osmanabad, Gulbarga, Bidar and Nanded. Smith (1950) cited 50,000–200,000. Report suppressed until c. 2013.
sources: Sunderlal Committee (1948/49): 27,000–40,000 killed in cold blood
Wilfred Cantwell Smith, Middle Eastern Journal 1950: 50,000–200,000
Indian military accounts: 807 Hyderabad soldiers and 1,373 Razakars killed; Indian Army losses very low
BBC, 24 Sep 2013; Sunil Purushotham research bringing report into public view

conflicts.name: Telangana peasant armed struggle
conflicts.summary: CPI-led peasant war against jagirdari, vetti and the Nizam, continuing after Operation Polo against the Indian Union until the 1951 CPI withdrawal. Ideological ancestor of later Naxalism, not organizationally continuous. Death totals not reliably censused.
sources: Standard histories of Telangana armed struggle; fatality census lacking

conflicts.name: Annexation of Goa, Daman and Diu
conflicts.summary: Indian armed forces seized Portuguese India in 36 hours. India: liberation of colonial territory. Portugal until 1974: aggression against national soil. 22 Indian and about 30 Portuguese killed; 4,668 captured. Portugal recognized Indian sovereignty in 1974.
sources: Indian official: 22 killed, 225 wounded
Portuguese: ~30 killed, 57 wounded, 4,668 captured

conflicts.name: Naga insurgency
conflicts.summary: Longest-running armed conflict in independent India. NNC declared independence 14 August 1947 (claim India never accepted). AFSPA 1958 first written for this theater. Nagaland statehood 1963 did not end the war. Shillong Accord 1975 split the movement; NSCN 1980 split 1988 into IM and K. IM ceasefire 1997; Framework Agreement 2015 unsigned in public and stalled on flag, constitution and territorial integration. UCDP cites ~20,000 deaths over four decades including factional and civilian targeting. SATP Nagaland-state slice since 2000 is much lower (~830) because much fighting was in Manipur/Assam/Myanmar.
peoples: Nagas (multiple tribes: Angami, Ao, Sema/Sumi, Tangkhul, Konyak, Hemi and others)
neighbouring Kuki, Meitei, Assamese populations as targets of Nagalim claims
sources: UCDP state-based Naga conflict narrative: ~20,000 over four decades
SATP Nagaland 2000–~2023: 830 fatalities in the state (191 civilians, 22 SF, 603 militants)
Shillong Accord 11 Nov 1975; NSCN-IM ceasefire 1 Aug 1997; Framework Agreement 3 Aug 2015
Indian Express explainer on Nagalim map ~120,000 km2 vs Nagaland 16,527 km2

conflicts.name: AFSPA / Disturbed Areas legal regime
aliases: Armed Forces (Jammu and Kashmir) Special Powers Act 1990
conflicts.summary: Emergency statute authorizing armed forces in notified 'disturbed areas' to fire to kill, arrest without warrant, and enjoy prior-sanction immunity (Section 6). Designed for Naga Hills as temporary; still in force in shrinking polygons. Punjab and J&K received sister laws. EEVFAM (SC 2016) held Manipur was not at war and fake encounters can be prosecuted; Oting (2021) showed sanction is still rarely granted. Not itself a campaign of violence but the legal geography of several campaigns.
sources: Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958
EEVFAM v. Union of India (2016) 8 SCC 1
MHA notifications shrinking disturbed areas from ~2015; Tripura withdrawal 2015; Meghalaya 2018

conflicts.name: Sino-Indian War
conflicts.summary: PLA offensive in Aksai Chin (west) and NEFA (east). China claims much of Arunachal as 'South Tibet'; India claims Aksai Chin. PLA ceased fire and withdrew in the east to north of the McMahon Line while retaining Aksai Chin. Border remains undemarcated.
peoples: Ladakhis — as resident populations, not combatant parties
sources: Indian Defence Ministry / Parliament: 1,383 killed, 1,047 wounded, 1,696 missing, 3,968 captured
Chinese official military history: 722 killed, 1,697 wounded
Chinese sources on Indian losses: ~4,897 killed or wounded plus 3,968 captured
COW #160: 1,353 Indian and 500 Chinese battle deaths
Henderson Brooks–Bhagat report (1963) still classified; Maxwell leak 2014

conflicts.name: Nathu La and Cho La clashes
conflicts.summary: Artillery and infantry clashes on the Sikkim–Tibet frontier. Smaller than 1962; both sides claim tactical success. Fatality figures diverge and are not independently censused.
sources: Indian and Chinese official narratives; no agreed body count

conflicts.name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1965
conflicts.summary: Pakistani infiltration into Kashmir (Gibraltar) and armour thrust (Grand Slam); India opened the international border toward Lahore. UN ceasefire 23 September; Tashkent Declaration 10 January 1966. Military stalemate; LoC unchanged.
externalSupport: US/UK arms embargo on both; Soviet Tashkent mediation
sources: COW Inter-State War #166
Indian official military deaths commonly ~3,000; Pakistani official in a similar band (~3,800 in some compilations)
Civilian border deaths poorly enumerated

conflicts.name: Rann of Kutch clashes
conflicts.summary: Prelude to the 1965 war in the Rann of Kutch. British-mediated ceasefire. Boundary later partly settled by tribunal (1968).
sources: UK-mediated ceasefire documents; Indian and Pakistani official histories

conflicts.name: Mizo National Front uprising
states: Mizo Hills / Mizoram (then Assam district, later UT, then state)
conflicts.summary: MNF launched Operation Jericho after the 1959 Mautam famine and perceived neglect. IAF strafed Aizawl 4–5 March 1966 — only use of Indian air power on a domestic population. Village grouping collapsed inhabited villages from 730 to 229 (1961–71). Mizoram Peace Accord 30 June 1986; statehood 1987. Widely cited as India's most successful insurgency settlement. Direct bombing deaths often ~13; SATP cites ~350 civilians killed by MNF in named phases and 59 SF in the 1966 recapture.
actors: Mizo National Front / Mizo National Army
sources: Mizoram Peace Accord, 30 June 1986
SATP Mizoram backgrounder: 95 MNA killed and 59 SF in 1966 recapture; ~350 civilians killed by MNF in cited phases
J.V. Hluna: ~13 killed as direct result of Aizawl bombing
Hazarika / Frontline 2026: inhabited villages 730→229 (1961–71)
Village grouping: 516 of 764 villages in some counts

conflicts.name: Bombing of Aizawl
conflicts.summary: IAF Toofani and Hunter aircraft strafed and bombed Aizawl and other Mizo towns during the MNF uprising. Unique in independent India. Direct fatalities low (~13 in one scholarly count) relative to displacement and political effect.
sources: Hluna and local histories; SATP timeline; Wikipedia compilation of IAF use

conflicts.name: Naxalbari uprising
conflicts.summary: Sharecropper revolt in Naxalbari, Darjeeling district, led to the CPI(ML) and the generic label 'Naxalite'. Small in deaths; large as lineage for the later Maoist belt.
sources: Standard histories of Naxalbari; UCDP CPI-ML successor conflicts from later decades

conflicts.name: Operation Steeplechase
conflicts.summary: Joint Army–paramilitary–police campaign against CPI(ML) in 1971. Broke the first Naxal wave in the plains. Fatality totals not in a single official public census.
sources: Secondary histories of the first Naxal wave; parliamentary and press accounts

conflicts.name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1971 / Bangladesh Liberation War
conflicts.summary: Crisis began with Operation Searchlight in East Pakistan (25 March 1971). ~10 million refugees entered India. Formal India–Pakistan war 3–16 December after Pakistani air strikes. Surrender in Dhaka; ~93,000 Pakistani POWs. Simla Agreement 1972. Civilian deaths in East Pakistan (300,000–3,000,000, fiercely disputed) occurred outside the Republic of India but drove Indian intervention and later Assam demography politics. Indian military deaths often ~3,843.
externalSupport: India to Mukti Bahini; US/China diplomatic tilt toward Pakistan (claim in Indian and Bangladeshi narratives)
sources: COW #178
Indian official military deaths ~3,843
Pakistani military deaths ~8,000–9,000 plus ~93,000 POWs
East Pakistan civilian deaths: Bangladesh official 3 million; scholarly range commonly 300,000–3,000,000 (Rummel, Bass, Bose disagree)
Refugee inflow to India ~10 million (UNHCR/contemporary estimates)

conflicts.name: Manipur valley insurgency
conflicts.summary: Valley-based Meitei groups (UNLF 1964, PLA/RPF 1978, PREPAK, KYKL, KCP) seeking independence or radical change, historically with China/Myanmar training. Parallel to Naga and Kuki armed groups in the hills. EEVFAM compiled 1,528 alleged extra-judicial killings. UNLF peace agreement 29 November 2023 did not end ethnic war. Fatalities were in decline to historic lows in 2020–22 (SATP: 7 in 2022) before the 2023 ethnic explosion.
externalSupport: China (historical training — Indian/security-source claim for later years)
sources: SATP Manipur assessments: 7 fatalities in 2022 (historic low since 1992)
EEVFAM v. UOI (2016): 1,528 alleged extra-judicial killings compiled by petitioners
UNLF–GoI–Manipur agreement 29 Nov 2023
MHA annual reports on valley-based groups

conflicts.name: Ahmedabad riots 1969
conflicts.summary: Major Hindu–Muslim riots in Ahmedabad. Deaths commonly cited around 500 or more. A landmark in Gujarat's riot history before 2002.
sources: Varshney–Wilkinson riot dataset; Reddy Commission; contemporary press. Exact official total varies by table.

conflicts.name: Tripura insurgency
conflicts.summary: Indigenous Tripuri (Borok) armed groups against a Bengali settler majority produced by Partition and 1971. TNV accord 1988; NLFT and ATTF continued from Bangladesh camps. SATP-era peak 2000: 514 fatalities (453 civilians). AFSPA withdrawn 2015. NLFT+ATTF memorandum 4 September 2024; 328+ cadres surrendered. Residual risk not zero but the armed campaign is treated as ended by the parties.
sources: SATP: 514 fatalities in 2000; NLFT-associated ~785 and ATTF ~314 over the SATP series (not strictly additive)
MHA: AFSPA withdrawn 27 May 2015; NLFT-SD 2019; NLFT+ATTF MoS 4 Sep 2024
Indian Express 9 Sep 2024: 328 cadres surrendered

conflicts.name: Assam Movement
conflicts.summary: AASU/AAGSP agitation to detect and deport 'foreigners' (primarily suspected Bangladeshi migrants). Official movement deaths often ~855–860 excluding or beside Nellie. Ended with Assam Accord 15 August 1985 (1966 and 24 March 1971 cut-offs). Did not resolve the citizenship question; NRC 2019 excluded 1.9 million.
sources: Assam Accord 15 August 1985
Official agitation deaths often ~855–860 (Economic Times timeline and others)
NRC 2019: 1.9 million excluded (not a death count)

conflicts.name: ULFA insurgency
conflicts.summary: Founded 1979 for Assamese sovereignty. Operations Bajrang (1990) and Rhino (1991); Bhutan Operation All Clear 2003 against camps; Bangladesh crackdown late 2000s. Split into pro-talks (Rajkhowa) and ULFA-Independent (Paresh Baruah). MoS 29 December 2023 with pro-talks ULFA; ULFA-I not a party and remains armed. Thousands of deaths over four decades (SATP Assam tables); no single authoritative total.
peoples: Bengali-origin communities as targets in some campaigns
externalSupport: Myanmar/China reported sanctuary for ULFA-I (Indian and some Western claims)
sources: SATP Assam/ULFA assessments
MHA: ULFA pro-talks MoS 29 Dec 2023
Royal Bhutan Army Operation All Clear, Dec 2003

conflicts.name: Bodo autonomy and insurgency
conflicts.summary: ABSU statehood demand from 1987; BLT; failed 1993 BAC; BTC accord 2003; NDFB factions including anti-talks Songbijit. Interleaved Bodo–Muslim and Bodo–Adivasi massacres (1993, 1994, 2008, 2012, 2014) with tens to hundreds dead per episode. Bodo Peace Accord 27 January 2020; 1,615 cadres surrendered. Residual criminal/political violence possible; the main armed campaign is treated as settled by the 2020 parties.
actors: NDFB (Ranjan Daimary, Songbijit, Progressive, DNR factions)
externalSupport: Bangladesh/Bhutan camps for some NDFB factions (historical)
sources: BTC accord 2003; Bodo Peace Accord 27 Jan 2020
MHA: 1,615 NDFB cadres surrendered 30 Jan 2020
Episode death tolls (2012, 2014) in press/NHRC — hundreds, not a single series

conflicts.name: Nellie massacre
conflicts.summary: About six hours in 14 villages of then Nagaon (now Morigaon). Official ~1,800 dead; commonly 2,000–3,000 Bengali-origin Muslims, mostly women and children. Tewary Commission (tabled 2025): 3,023 killed in 11 Assam districts January–April 1983, 1,811 in Nagaon. Tiwa (Lalung) and other locals as attackers during a boycotted election. 688 FIRs; cases dropped after the Assam Accord. Generally not a UCDP ACD armed conflict.
sources: Official Nellie ~1,800
Common scholarly/press range 2,000–3,000
Tewary Commission (tabled Assam Assembly 25 Nov 2025): 3,023 statewide Jan–Apr 1983; 1,811 Nagaon
Harsh Mander / Centre for Equity Studies; Baruah
688 FIRs; 378 closed for lack of evidence; remainder dropped after Accord

conflicts.name: Punjab / Khalistan insurgency
conflicts.summary: Sikh militant campaign for Khalistan and/or radical autonomy after the Anandpur Sahib agitation. UCDP conflict from 1983. Operation Blue Star (June 1984) and November 1984 anti-Sikh pogroms (separate node) transformed the conflict. SATP/Gill: 21,469 killed in a little over a decade. Majority of civilian victims of militants were Sikh (SATP: 7,139 of 11,694). Police counter-insurgency associated with disappearances (Ensaaf/HRW). Militancy suppressed by ~1993; diaspora plots continue at low level.
externalSupport: Pakistan (Indian official claim for later phase; Pakistan denies)
sources: UCDP conflict India: Punjab/Khalistan (351)
SATP Punjab backgrounder: 21,469 lives
SATP: 11,694 civilians killed by Sikh militant groups, of whom 7,139 Sikhs
Rajiv–Longowal Accord 1985; Longowal assassinated

conflicts.name: Operation Blue Star
conflicts.summary: Indian Army assault on the Harmandir Sahib complex to dislodge Bhindranwale and armed followers. Government White Paper: 493 civilians/militants and 83 soldiers killed. Independent and Sikh organizations: 3,000–8,000 including pilgrims — unverifiable; no independent body count. Followed by mutinies in some Sikh units and, after Indira Gandhi's assassination, the November pogroms.
sources: Government of India White Paper on the Punjab Agitation: 493 civilians/militants, 83 soldiers
SATP/Gill: more than 100 Army dead and over 550 civilians in crossfire (their wording)
Ensaaf and Sikh organizations: 3,000–8,000 — disputed, unverifiable

conflicts.name: Anti-Sikh violence of November 1984
conflicts.summary: After Indira Gandhi's assassination by Sikh bodyguards, organized mobs killed Sikhs in Delhi and other cities. Nanavati/official Delhi: 2,733. National estimates often 3,000–4,000. Citizen inquiries and HRW document voter lists, kerosene, and Congress local organizers; police inaction. Few convictions. Not UCDP ACD 'armed conflict'.
actors: Congress local organizers (Nanavati and citizen inquiries — contested by some accused)
sources: Nanavati Commission / official Delhi death toll 2,733
HRW and citizen inquiries: national figure often ~3,000–4,000
PUCL/PUDR Who Are the Guilty (1984)

conflicts.name: Air India Flight 182 bombing
conflicts.summary: Bomb destroyed Air India Flight 182; 329 killed. Attributed to Babbar Khalsa conspiracy in Canada. GTD terrorism event linked to the Khalistan campaign.
peoples: mostly Canadian and Indian civilians of several faiths
sources: Canadian inquiries and trials; GTD; 329 dead

conflicts.name: Siachen conflict
conflicts.summary: India occupied Saltoro Ridge in April 1984 beyond map point NJ9842. Pakistan holds lower approaches. Most deaths from weather, altitude and avalanches. Indian official weather-related deaths >1,100 by 2019; combined deaths often cited ~2,000+. Pakistan's 2012 Gayari avalanche killed 129 soldiers and 11 civilians. Firing reduced after 2003 ceasefire; deployment continues. Both states claim; China is adjacent via the 1963 Shaksgam agreement (India does not recognize).
sources: Indian government acknowledgement June 2019: weather-related deaths crossed 1,100
Secondary combined estimates ~2,000+
Gayari avalanche 6–7 Apr 2012: 129 Pakistani soldiers + 11 civilians
Combat share often estimated under 5%

conflicts.name: Sumdorong Chu standoff
conflicts.summary: PLA and Indian forward deployments in the Tawang tract. Few or no combat deaths; high mobilisation. De-escalated without a boundary settlement.
sources: Indian and Chinese military histories; contemporary press

conflicts.name: Kashmir insurgency
conflicts.summary: Armed campaign from 1988–89 after the disputed 1987 election. JKLF (independence) then Hizbul Mujahideen, Lashkar-e-Taiba, Jaish-e-Mohammed and others. India: Pakistani proxy war. Pakistan: indigenous uprising plus moral support. UCDP lumps rebels as 'Kashmir insurgents'. MHA via SATP 1990–2017: 44,567 deaths (13,979 civilians, 5,131 SF, 25,457 'terrorists'). SATP news compilation 1988–2012 ~43,300. Disappearances and encounter killings are a parallel HRW/APDP series not identical to MHA. Article 370 revoked 5 August 2019. Intensity far below 1990s–2002 peaks but not zero.
externalSupport: Pakistan (Indian and many Western governments: ISI-backed; Pakistan: denial of official direction)
sources: UCDP conflict 364 India: Kashmir
MHA table via SATP, 1990–2017: 44,567 total
SATP 1988–2012 compilation ~43,314
UCDP: war-intensity years around 2000–2002; 2024 among lowest since 1989

conflicts.name: Kashmiri Pandit exodus
conflicts.summary: Targeted killings and threats in 1989–90 led most Valley Pandits to leave. Government lists often ~219–399 killed in the early years; Pandit organizations cite higher. Displacement commonly 100,000–140,000 (some claims to 300,000). Pandit groups and much Indian official memory: ethnic cleansing. Some Valley political actors: migration amid general chaos. Record both claims. IDP camps in Jammu persisted for decades.
sources: J&K government / MHA lists of Pandits killed: often ~219–399 for the early phase
Pandit organizations: higher killing counts and 100,000–300,000 displaced
Scholarly range on displacement commonly ~100,000–140,000 from the Valley

conflicts.name: Hashimpura massacre
conflicts.summary: Provincial Armed Constabulary personnel detained and killed 42 Muslim men from Hashimpura, Meerut, dumping bodies in canals. Convictions decades later. One-sided state violence, not a two-sided riot.
sources: Court records; 42 killed; PUCL/HRW accounts

conflicts.name: Bhagalpur riots
conflicts.summary: Hindu–Muslim violence in Bhagalpur during the Ramjanmabhoomi mobilisation. Deaths commonly ~1,000. Among the deadliest riots of the 1980s.
sources: Inquiry commission and press; ~1,000 deaths commonly cited; Varshney–Wilkinson

conflicts.name: Kuki–Naga conflict in Manipur
conflicts.summary: Inter-tribal war in Manipur's hills as NSCN-IM asserted Nagalim and Kuki groups resisted. Hundreds killed; large village emptying. Under-imported into national datasets. Displacement in contemporary reports sometimes put above 100,000 — flag uncertainty. Sets up later SoO Kuki groups and 2023 hill politics.
sources: Contemporary NE press and SATP notes; death toll in the hundreds to around 1,000 — no single census
Displacement figures vary widely; treat high-end 100,000+ as uncertain

conflicts.name: Babri Masjid demolition and Bombay riots
conflicts.summary: Demolition of Babri Masjid in Ayodhya triggered nationwide riots. Bombay (Dec 1992–Jan 1993) was the worst urban episode: about 900 dead. Srikrishna Commission: December phase as largely leaderless Muslim reaction; January as Hindu attacks led by Shiv Sena, with communally inciting press. National death toll in the thousands (no single official all-India table). March 1993 Bombay blasts (257 dead) were a sequel, coded separately as terrorism.
actors: kar sevaks / VHP/BJP/RSS ecosystem at Ayodhya
sources: Srikrishna Commission Report (1998): Bombay ~900; commonly cited split 575 Muslim, 275 Hindu, 50 other
Liberhan Commission on the demolition
UCDP non-state Hindus–Muslims active in this period

conflicts.name: Bombay serial blasts 1993
conflicts.summary: Coordinated bombs in Bombay killing 257. Courts linked Dawood Ibrahim / Memon network. Treated by prosecutors as revenge for the 1992–93 riots. GTD event.
externalSupport: Pakistan (Indian official and court claims; Pakistan denies)
sources: TADA court judgments; 257 dead; GTD

conflicts.name: Meghalaya insurgencies
conflicts.summary: Khasi HNLC and Garo ANVC/GNLA campaigns. Fatalities in the low hundreds over the 2000s, then near zero. ANVC accord 2014 (751 surrendered). GNLA crushed ~2018. AFSPA withdrawn 2018. HNLC talks on/off.
peoples: non-tribal settlers as targets in some campaigns
sources: MHA: ANVC MoS 24 Sep 2014; 751 surrendered 15 Dec 2014
SATP Meghalaya: fatalities near zero after 2018; AFSPA withdrawn 2018

conflicts.name: Kargil War
conflicts.summary: Pakistani Northern Light Infantry occupied posts on the Indian side of the LoC. Pakistan initially described fighters as militants. India recaptured positions by 26 July. First conventional war after 1998 nuclear tests.
externalSupport: US/Clinton diplomacy pressing Pakistan to withdraw
sources: COW #223
Indian MoD / Kargil Review Committee: 527 killed, 1,363 wounded (named)
Pakistan official 357; Nawaz Sharif later said over 4,000; independent range often 400–4,000

conflicts.name: Attack on the Indian Parliament
conflicts.summary: Armed assault on Parliament. Nine killed plus attackers (counts vary slightly by whether attackers are included). India attributed to JeM/LeT; led to Operation Parakram mobilisation. Convictions including Afzal Guru remain legally and politically contested.
sources: Court records; MHA; GTD; 9 security/civilian dead plus attackers in most official counts

conflicts.name: Operation Parakram
conflicts.summary: Full-scale mobilisation after the Parliament attack. No full war. Deaths from mines, accidents and LoC fire in the hundreds (no single agreed total). High economic and nuclear-risk cost.
sources: Indian Army / press on accidental and mine deaths; no COW war

conflicts.name: Gujarat violence 2002
conflicts.summary: After the Godhra train fire (59 karsevaks; accident vs attack still disputed), statewide anti-Muslim violence. Official: 1,044 dead (790 Muslim, 254 Hindu) plus 223 missing. Concerned Citizens Tribunal: 1,926. Other estimates 2,000+. CCT and many human-rights groups: organized pogrom with state complicity — contested by the then state government and later courts in some cases. Sexual violence extensively documented. ~150,000 in relief camps at peak in some tabulations. UCDP non-state Hindus–Muslims active year; not an ACD war.
actors: VHP/Bajrang Dal (CCT and many HR reports)
sources: Government of Gujarat / NHRC response: 1,044 dead (790 Muslim, 254 Hindu), 223 missing, 2,500+ injured
Concerned Citizens Tribunal 2002 (Justices Krishna Iyer, Sawant, Suresh et al.): 1,926
Other HR estimates 2,000+
CJP map notes: 132,532 displaced (2002 figure on their sheet)
UCDP non-state Hindus (India)–Muslims (India)

conflicts.name: Godhra train fire
conflicts.summary: Coach S-6 of the Sabarmati Express burned at Godhra; 59 karsevaks dead. Nanavati-Mehta Commission: conspiracy. Banerjee Committee and CCT: accident. Courts convicted some Muslim accused. Spark of Gujarat 2002; cause still a competing-frame object.
sources: 59 dead (agreed)
Nanavati-Mehta: conspiracy
Banerjee Committee / CCT: accident

conflicts.name: Naxalite–Maoist insurgency
conflicts.summary: From Naxalbari 1967 through PWG and MCC to CPI (Maoist) merger 21 September 2004. Peak late 2000s: ~150–180 districts listed affected; SATP 1,180 fatalities in 2010 (MHA 1,005). MHA RTI 2014: 12,183 civilians+SF killed by Naxals 1993–2013 in nine states (excludes Maoists killed). SATP 2000–Nov 2022 ~11,073 total including Maoists. Salwa Judum (2005–11) as state-backed militia, invalidated by SC 2011. Government 2024–26 claims near-end; UCDP 2025 still lists CPI-Maoist as India's most intense state-based dyad that year. Treat 'Naxal-free' as a government claim.
externalSupport: ideological links to foreign Maoist groups (limited material)
sources: MHA RTI via PTI 12 Mar 2014: 12,183 civilians+SF killed by Naxals ~1993–2013
MHA: 2010 incidents 1,936 and deaths (civ+SF) 1,005; 2024 incidents 374 and deaths 150
SATP/wiki compilation 2000–2025: ~4,134 civilians, 2,722 SF, ~5,000 Maoists
UCDP India 2025 narrative: CPI-Maoist most intense dyad

conflicts.name: Salwa Judum
conflicts.summary: State-supported (and later denied-as-such) civilian militia in Dantewada/Bijapur against Maoists. Mass village displacement. Supreme Court 2011 held arming of tribals as SPOs unconstitutional. Casualties and IDPs not in a single official census; ethnographic work (Sundar) is the core source.
sources: Nandini Sundar; PUCL; SC judgment 2011 on SPOs/Salwa Judum
Displacement of hundreds of villages — figures vary by NGO vs state

conflicts.name: Dantewada CRPF ambush
conflicts.summary: CPI (Maoist) ambush killed 76 security personnel (mostly CRPF) in Dantewada. Single worst SF loss of the campaign; sits inside the 2010 peak year.
sources: MHA / CRPF: 76 killed

conflicts.name: Kandhamal violence
conflicts.summary: Anti-Christian violence in Kandhamal after the killing of Swami Laxmanananda. Official deaths ~38–40; Christian groups 100+. Large displacement of Christians. Scale small by death threshold, politically large.
sources: Official ~38–40; church/HR 100+; NHRC/press

conflicts.name: Mumbai attacks 26 November 2008
conflicts.summary: LeT fidayeen assault on multiple Mumbai sites. 166 dead. US and Indian courts (Headley, Kasab) documented Pakistan-based controllers. Linked to the Kashmir militant field though the attacks were in Mumbai.
externalSupport: Pakistan-based LeT infrastructure (US and Indian judicial findings; Pakistan official denial of state direction)
sources: Indian official 166 dead; GTD; US District Court (Headley); Kasab trial

conflicts.name: Muzaffarnagar riots
conflicts.summary: Jat–Muslim violence in Muzaffarnagar/Shamli. Official 62 dead; other estimates around 100. Tens of thousands displaced (often ~50,000). UCDP non-state Hindus–Muslims active year.
sources: Official 62 deaths
Other estimates ~100
Displacement often cited ~40,000–50,000
UCDP non-state 2013

conflicts.name: Pulwama attack and Balakot crisis
states: Pakistan (Balakot — Indian claim of target location)
conflicts.summary: JeM suicide VBIED killed 40 CRPF personnel at Pulwama. India struck at Balakot, Pakistan; aerial engagement the next day. Casualty claims on the Pakistani side of the strike are incompatible across governments. Not a COW war.
sources: Indian official: 40 CRPF at Pulwama; Balakot battle-damage assessments disputed

conflicts.name: Delhi riots 2020
conflicts.summary: Lethal Hindu–Muslim violence in north-east Delhi during CAA/NRC protests. Police: 53 dead, majority Muslim. UCDP non-state Hindus–Muslims active year. Fact-finding groups allege police bias; police and some political actors allege a pre-planned riot — competing frames.
sources: Delhi Police: 53 dead
UCDP non-state 2020
Fact-finding reports (DU, PUCL and others) vs police chargesheets — disagreement on initiation

conflicts.name: Galwan clash
conflicts.summary: First lethal PLA–Indian Army clash since 1975, during a broader 2020 Ladakh standoff. Fought without firearms per both official accounts (clubs, stones). India: 20 killed. China: 4 killed (PLA Daily 2021). Indian media claimed 25–40+ Chinese — unverified. Part of a larger mobilisation, not a 1962-scale war. Disengagement at some points 2024.
sources: Indian Army 16 June 2020: 20 killed
PLA Daily 2021: 4 Chinese killed
Indian media 25–40+ Chinese — unverified

conflicts.name: Oting killings
conflicts.summary: 21 Para SF fired on a pickup of coal miners at Oting, Mon district; six died on the spot. Subsequent clash with villagers raised the civilian toll to 13–14 plus one soldier. Centre denied AFSPA Section 6 prosecution sanction (2023); Supreme Court quashed criminal proceedings (2024). Became the focal AFSPA legitimacy crisis of the 2020s in Nagaland.
sources: Nagaland SIT chargesheet; 13–14 civilians and 1 soldier dead in the episode
MoD denied sanction Feb 2023; SC Sep 2024 closed proceedings absent sanction

conflicts.name: Kuki–Meitei conflict in Manipur
conflicts.summary: Ethnic war between Meitei (valley) and Kuki-Zo (hills) from 3 May 2023 after a High Court recommendation on Meitei ST status and a tribal solidarity march. Deeper drivers: hill land/forest/poppy, Myanmar refugee inflow, majoritarian vs indigenous claims. Governor Feb 2024: 219 killed. Later official compilations: 306 by Sep 2026; 60,000+ displaced; thousands of houses and hundreds of churches/temples damaged. Population sorted into ethnically homogenous zones. SATP: 163 insurgency-linked fatalities in Manipur in 2023 vs 7 in 2022. UNLF signed a peace deal in Nov 2023 even as the ethnic war continued. ACLED 2026 also records spreading Kuki–Naga hill violence.
actors: Meitei militias (Arambai Tenggol, Meitei Leepun — widely named in reporting)
Kuki-Zo village volunteers and SoO-linked groups (role disputed)
valley insurgent groups (UNLF/PLA etc. — security-source claims of involvement)
externalSupport: Myanmar conflict as refugee/weapons context (not a state patron)
sources: Manipur Governor 28 Feb 2024: 219 killed since May 2023
SATP 2023: 163 insurgency-linked fatalities in Manipur (72 civilians, 73 'terrorists', 17 SF)
Government figures compiled to Sep 2026: 306 dead, 60,000+ displaced (Wikipedia citing official)
MHA annual report 2023: Manipur 187 of 243 NE violent incidents
Al Jazeera May 2026: >250 dead, tens of thousands displaced, 58,000 still in camps

conflicts.name: Pahalgam attack
conflicts.summary: Gunmen killed 26 people, almost all male tourists, at Baisaran meadow near Pahalgam on 22 April 2025. Indian authorities and USCIRF: 25 Indian citizens and one Nepalese national; most Hindu men. The Resistance Front (described by India as an LeT offshoot) claimed responsibility; India attributed the attack to Pakistan-based groups (Pakistan denies). Trigger for Operation Sindoor.
actors: The Resistance Front / LeT (claim and Indian attribution)
peoples: one local Muslim pony handler among the dead in several reports
sources: Indian Express / India Today / CNN / Al Jazeera / USCIRF April 2025: 26 killed, named victim lists
TRF claim of responsibility; India: LeT front created after 2019
Trigger for Operation Sindoor (PIB May 2025)

conflicts.name: Operation Sindoor
conflicts.summary: Indian named operation after Pahalgam. Cross-border strikes and Pakistani retaliation 7–10 May 2025. PIB: nine sites targeted. BBC (July 2025) described 'dozens' killed in the four-day confrontation, the bloodiest in decades, before a US-announced ceasefire. Fatality claims still diverge across governments. Treat as interstate crisis, not a COW war, until datasets code it.
sources: PIB 7 May 2025 on Operation Sindoor
Casualty figures remain disputed across governments; do not invent a total

conflicts.name: Manipur extra-judicial killings cases (EEVFAM)
conflicts.summary: Not a single campaign but a documented pattern. EEVFAM compiled 1,528 alleged extra-judicial executions by police and security forces. Supreme Court 2016 held Manipur was not at war, rejected blanket AFSPA immunity, and ordered inquiry/CBI investigation in sampled cases. Outcome of prosecutions remains limited. Include as a harm series overlapping the valley insurgency.
sources: EEVFAM v. Union of India (2016); petitioner compilation 1,528 cases
